nodes.description: Pejvakin is expressed in the cell bodies of neurons along the afferent auditory pathway, including all spiral ganglion neurons of the human cochlea, where it is also found in nuclei. The first DFNB59 families had auditory neuropathy, and mice homozygous for the patient R183W variant have abnormal auditory brainstem responses. Whether pejvakin is required in neurons is contested, because neuron-specific deletion did not impair hearing in another mouse study.

nodes.description: Biallelic germline PJVK variants, missense and frameshift, remove pejvakin function. Pejvakin is a 352-residue gasdermin-family protein, a paralog of DFNA5. It binds LC3B through an LC3-interacting region and is proposed to act as a redox-activated receptor for pexophagy; its two C-terminal cysteines, C328 and C343, are needed for the LC3B interaction and for pexophagy. The patient variant p.C343S replaces one of them.

nodes.description: Pejvakin-deficient cochleas show marked oxidative stress and impaired antioxidant defences, and their hair-cell peroxisomes become structurally abnormal after the onset of hearing. Hair cells and auditory pathway neurons of pejvakin-deficient mice and of patients are exceptionally vulnerable to sound. Pejvakin-deficient mice have variable auditory phenotypes, and their hearing thresholds correlated with the number of pups per cage, suggesting that even pup vocalizations may be harmful. The process is bound as response to oxidative stress with a DECREASED modifier because the lesion is the failed antioxidant response; it is the oxidative stress itself that increases.

nodes.description: Pejvakin is associated with peroxisomes. In wild-type mice, noise rapidly raises cochlear Pjvk transcription, triggers peroxisome proliferation in hair cells and primary auditory neurons, and induces selective autophagic degradation of peroxisomes (pexophagy) in hair cells. In pejvakin-deficient mice, noise does not induce pexophagy and peroxisomes fail to proliferate.

nodes.description: In mice, pejvakin is needed in hair cells, and in outer hair cells specifically, for normal hearing. Deleting Pjvk in all hair cells or only in outer hair cells causes early-onset profound hearing loss, and deleting it in adult outer hair cells causes slowly progressive hearing loss with outer hair cell degeneration followed by inner hair cell loss. Pejvakin's C-terminal domain binds ROCK2 and IQGAP1, which points to a role in Rho signalling.

nodes.description: Sound damages the auditory system of pejvakin-deficient mice and patients far more than normal. Pejvakin-deficient mice have variable hearing thresholds that correlated with the number of pups per cage, suggesting that even everyday sound such as pup vocalizations may be harmful.
